sleepers.name: Ty Jerome
sleepers.why: 8 articles across 5 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, Hashtag Basketball, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He averaged 19.7 points and 5.7 assists in 22.6 minutes over 15 games and has the inside track to start now that Ja Morant is in Portland. Hashtag projects him 62nd against an ADP near 110. Durability is the catch.

sleepers.name: Zach Edey
sleepers.why: 6 articles across 4 outlets (ESPN, Hashtag Basketball, NBC Sports, RotoWire). Hashtag projects him 36th against an ADP near 75, and RotoWire's Alex Barutha says fear of his injuries has him going about 25 picks after Donovan Clingan. He played 11 games last season and is ramping up from March elbow and ankle surgeries; NBC Sports calls him risk/reward.

sleepers.name: Kel'el Ware
sleepers.why: 6 articles across 4 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, FantasyPros, RotoWire). He went to Milwaukee in the Giannis trade and posted 18 points, 15 rebounds and 3.1 stocks per 36. He supplies blocks, threes and field-goal percentage, though Myles Turner still clouds the minutes.

sleepers.name: Derrick White
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 4 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). Jaylen Brown's exit makes him Boston's second scorer, and he adds threes, assists, steals and guard blocks. He shot a career-worst 39.4% last year and still finished 30th in 9-cat.

sleepers.name: OG Anunoby
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 4 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He finished 36th in 9-cat last season and goes around pick 68 on Yahoo. He played at least 67 games in each of his three top-40 seasons.

sleepers.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, NBC Sports, RotoWire). The Nic Claxton trade makes him Brooklyn's starting center. He put up 16.8 points and 12.8 rebounds per 36 in seven starts, but has never averaged 19 minutes and RotoWire expects mid-20s, not 30.

sleepers.name: Ajay Mitchell
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe are gone, and his playoff minutes jumped from about 8 to 28.8. He goes after pick 100 on ESPN.

sleepers.name: Cedric Coward
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros, RotoWire). Memphis lost nearly 70% of its usage with Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. gone, and he shot well as an All-Rookie pick.

sleepers.name: Darius Garland
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He runs a thin Clippers offense while Brandon Ingram is out, and RotoWire and NBC Sports see top-25 to top-30 upside from a Yahoo ADP near 62. Injury history and possible late-season rest hold the price down.

sleepers.name: Walker Kessler
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, CBS, NBC Sports). He is the Lakers' starting center next to Luka Doncic on a four-year, $130 million deal, and SportsLine's model ranks him the No. 13 center against an ADP of 59. He played five games last season after shoulder surgery, and RotoWire calls him a major injury risk.

sleepers.name: Naz Reid
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, FantasyPros, NBC Sports). A full-time starter at power forward after Miles Bridges was traded, with 30-plus minutes expected. He has played 68 to 81 games in six straight seasons.

sleepers.name: Jaime Jaquez Jr.
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, FantasyPros, RotoWire). He should start in Milwaukee after the Giannis trade, coming off 15.4 points and 4.7 assists in 28 minutes.

sleepers.name: Caleb Wilson
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, FantasyPros, NBC Sports). The No. 4 pick starts at power forward and averaged 23.5 points and 2.5 blocks in Summer League, at an ADP near 80 to 96. FantasyPros warns about his free-throw shooting and turnovers.

sleepers.name: Ausar Thompson
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). Barutha's top category-league sleeper: elite steals and blocks with rebounds, and JB Bickerstaff expects his minutes to rise above 26. He shot 57.1% at the line with almost no threes, so he fits a punt-FT% build.

sleepers.name: Jalen Suggs
sleepers.why: 5 articles across 2 outlets (Hashtag Basketball, RotoWire). Top-50 per-game value last season at a Yahoo ADP near 107; Hashtag projects him 53rd. He has had one healthy season in five.

sleepers.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
sleepers.why: 4 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). He backs up both Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl and goes 139th on ESPN against 112th on Yahoo. A Poeltl injury would make him a major contributor.

sleepers.name: Ayo Dosunmu
sleepers.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). He leads Minnesota's second unit and averaged 14.7 points in 34 games there, with more if Anthony Edwards or LaMelo Ball sits.

sleepers.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
sleepers.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (CBS, RotoWire). The No. 7 pick should start at point guard with 30-plus minutes after Russell Westbrook and DeMar DeRozan left. SportsLine's model ranks him above Trae Young; FantasyPros worries about his efficiency.

sleepers.name: Khaman Maluach
sleepers.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). Mark Williams' shoulder surgery opens the center job, and he has a Ware-like profile of dunks, rebounds, blocks and some threes.

sleepers.name: Immanuel Quickley
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). He was nearly a top-50 player in 70 games last season and goes outside the top 90; two outlets say Kawhi Leonard's arrival hurts him least.

sleepers.name: Ryan Rollins
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros). Milwaukee's starting point guard averaged 20.2 points and 6.1 assists in 25 games without Giannis. FantasyPros says draft him if he is outside the top 80.

sleepers.name: Coby White
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, RotoWire). He takes over the offense LaMelo Ball left on a three-year, $74 million deal. Both articles predate his calf strain, which now puts the opener in doubt.

sleepers.name: Nic Claxton
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). He has an uncontested starting job in Chicago with Josh Giddey feeding him. He is questionable for the opener with a hamstring strain.

sleepers.name: Cameron Johnson
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). More minutes and shots after Tim Hardaway Jr. left for Miami; he has never played more than 66 games.

sleepers.name: Grayson Allen
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (FantasyPros, RotoWire). A deep-league source of threes in Charlotte who may fill in for Kon Knueppel.

sleepers.name: Jaden McDaniels
sleepers.why: 3 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). Julius Randle and Naz Reid left, and he has two straight top-75 seasons with about 2.0 stocks at an ADP near 89.

sleepers.name: Cason Wallace
sleepers.why: 3 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). Three Thunder wings left, and he already averages 1.9 steals in 27 minutes at an ADP near 118.

sleepers.name: John Collins
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). He tops Detroit's power forward depth chart and goes around pick 116 on Yahoo.

sleepers.name: Julius Randle
sleepers.why: 2 articles across 1 outlet (ESPN). ESPN's Eric Karabell expects a return to about 24 points and 10 rebounds on a weak Nets roster. Athlon lists him among possible busts.

sleepers.name: Mitchell Robinson
sleepers.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (NBC Sports). NBC Sports gives him the inside track to start at center around pick 108. RotoWire disagrees and expects Neemias Queta to start, so this is a split call.

sleepers.name: Neemias Queta
sleepers.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). RotoWire's Adam King expects him to keep the starting job at about 26 minutes with a Yahoo ADP of 117. RotoWire's Jeff Edgerton and NBC Sports see a timeshare with Mitchell Robinson.

sleepers.name: Josh Hart
sleepers.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). He should start and play heavy minutes with Mitchell Robinson gone, at an ADP near 96. Athlon lists him among possible busts.

sleepers.name: Keegan Murray
sleepers.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (ESPN). He could log heavy minutes on a rebuilding roster, more so if Sabonis or LaVine is traded. He played 23 games last season.

sleepers.name: Peyton Watson
sleepers.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (ESPN). A likely starter in Cleveland with a strong block rate.

busts.name: Anthony Davis
busts.why: 5 articles across 4 outlets (ESPN, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He played 20 games last season and has topped 60 once in four years, and now shares usage with Trae Young and AJ Dybantsa. NBC Sports calls relying on him as your main big a major risk in any build.

busts.name: LeBron James
busts.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, FantasyPros, RotoWire). He turns 42 in December, played 60 games with a career-low 20.9 points, and projects as the fourth or fifth option on a team already planning his rest days. ADP is about 37 to 38.

busts.name: Joel Embiid
busts.why: 4 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros, RotoWire). He has played 57 of 164 games over two seasons, his rebounds and blocks fell to career lows, and the 76ers will manage his workload. NBC Sports is the dissent, calling him a possible steal in punt-turnover or punt-steal builds.

busts.name: De'Aaron Fox
busts.why: 3 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros, RotoWire). He is drafted near pick 65 to 80 with Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper squeezing his role; Harper outplayed him in the Finals.

busts.name: Ja Morant
busts.why: 3 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, RotoWire). He has played 79 games in three seasons, does not shoot threes, and may come off the bench behind Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday. NBC Sports is the dissent and likes him at an eighth-round price.

busts.name: Paolo Banchero
busts.why: 4 articles across 2 outlets (FantasyPros, RotoWire). Category leagues punish his 44.9% career shooting, 74.3% free throws, three-plus turnovers and thin steals and blocks, yet he goes around pick 34. Barutha is more forgiving because 25/7/5 lines are scarce.

busts.name: Kawhi Leonard
busts.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). His ADP slid from 25.8 to 31.4 because he is unlikely to repeat 27.9 points and has not reached 70 games since 2017. Barutha would only take him if he falls to about pick 45.

busts.name: Jaylen Brown
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros). His 35.1% usage will not carry over next to Embiid, Maxey and LeBron; Athlon estimates about 300 fewer shots. Yahoo ADP is about 30.

busts.name: Zion Williamson
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, ESPN). Even in a 62-game year he gave no threes, 5.7 rebounds and 0.5 blocks, and ESPN's Steve Alexander does not trust him past 50 games.

busts.name: Brandon Ingram
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Fantasy Alarm, RotoWire). He will miss the start of the season with a partially torn Achilles and no timetable; Fantasy Alarm leads its bust list with him.

busts.name: Nikola Vucevic
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, RotoWire). He is declining across the board, his games played have dropped three straight years, and he may not hold a rotation role in Orlando.

busts.name: Tyler Herro
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, RotoWire). Listed as a bust by two outlets without detailed reasoning; he played 33 games last season and had a foot procedure in April.

busts.name: Bam Adebayo
busts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). Giannis Antetokounmpo's arrival overlaps with his skill set, and Edgerton expects his numbers to drop.

busts.name: Cooper Flagg
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (CBS). SportsLine's model ranks him behind Banchero and Davis at an ADP of 10 because Kyrie Irving's return takes the ball out of his hands under a first-year coach. Four other outlets call him a breakout, so this is a minority view.

busts.name: VJ Edgecombe
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). The arrivals of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown cut into his touches more than anyone's.

busts.name: Jakob Poeltl
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (ESPN). ESPN's Jim McCormick says his price is inflated and Collin Murray-Boyles may take his minutes; he played 46 games last season.

busts.name: Dillon Brooks
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (Athlon). He faded after January, turns 31 and is a fourth or fifth option.

busts.name: Jalen Brunson
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). Barutha calls him a third- or fourth-round player in category leagues because he adds nothing on defense or the glass, against an ADP near 15 to 22.

busts.name: Josh Giddey
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). RotoWire rates him a better points-league pick because of weak defensive stats and shooting percentages.

busts.name: Damian Lillard
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (NBC Sports). NBC Sports says to wait until the later rounds given his age (36), the Achilles and an unclear role.

busts.name: Dereck Lively II
busts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (NBC Sports). NBC Sports says not to draft him outside deep leagues because his foot recovery has no timeline; ESPN had named him a breakout in September.

busts.name: Caleb Wilson
busts.why: Oct 18 preseason check. 3.4 turnovers and 55.6% FT (10-18) in 26.6 min over 5 games, after 33% FT in Summer League, and 4.6 rebounds against a 7.7 projection.

busts.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
busts.why: Oct 18 preseason check. 17.3 pts and 2 threes, but 3.5 turnovers in 24 min and 42% FG; took a backseat to Ben Simmons as primary ballhandler in the finale. RotoWire calls him a points-league player.

busts.name: AJ Dybantsa
busts.why: Oct 18 preseason check. Mild left ankle sprain in the Oct 16 finale (precautionary, no timeline). 43.9% FG and 61.9% FT on real volume, under one three a game.

breakouts.name: Brandon Miller
breakouts.why: 7 articles across 5 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He becomes Charlotte's first option with LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges gone. ESPN's Jim McCormick expects Paul George-like production.

breakouts.name: Dylan Harper
breakouts.why: 5 articles across 4 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He averaged 18 points off the bench in the Finals and three ESPN analysts named him a must-draft, though he is still behind Fox and Castle.

breakouts.name: Austin Reaves
breakouts.why: 5 articles across 4 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, FantasyPros, RotoWire). With LeBron James gone he becomes the Lakers' second option; he averaged about 28 points and 7 to 8 assists in games James missed.

breakouts.name: Cooper Flagg
breakouts.why: 5 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, RotoWire). He averaged 23.3 points over his last 50 games as a rookie and gets Kyrie Irving back to draw defenses. CBS's model is the lone dissent.

breakouts.name: Donovan Clingan
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 3 outlets (ESPN, NBC Sports, RotoWire). He played 77 games with 12.1 points, 11.6 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 27 minutes and now has an uncontested starting job.

breakouts.name: Anthony Black
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 3 outlets (Athlon, ESPN, NBC Sports). He had career highs in 40 starts last season and could push Jalen Suggs for the starting job; he currently has a sprained ankle.

breakouts.name: Kel'el Ware
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). ESPN and RotoWire both expect him to reach the top tier of centers once his role settles; his free-throw rate rose to 74%.

breakouts.name: Matas Buzelis
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). He jumped to 16.3 points in Year 2 and turns 22; his ADP slid from 59 to 65.

breakouts.name: Egor Demin
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, RotoWire). Named as a breakout candidate by three articles without detailed reasoning.

breakouts.name: Domantas Sabonis
breakouts.why: 3 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). NBC Sports expects a return to star form after a 19-game season, with trade risk attached.

breakouts.name: Walker Kessler
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). He averaged 14.4 points, 10.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks on 70% shooting in five games before surgery, and ESPN sees top-40 category upside if he stays healthy.

breakouts.name: Cedric Coward
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (ESPN, RotoWire). ESPN's Karabell thinks he can reach 20 points as a starter on a rebuilding team.

breakouts.name: Ryan Rollins
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (Athlon, FantasyPros). Athlon expects him to lead Milwaukee's offense with Tyler Herro after averaging 17.3 points and 5.6 assists.

breakouts.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (CBS, RotoWire). SportsLine's model names the rookie its top breakout.

breakouts.name: Jalen Williams
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 2 outlets (NBC Sports, RotoWire). NBC Sports expects a full bounce back from a 33-game season; his ADP rose from 43.6 to 41.

breakouts.name: Derrick White
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). Edgerton expects a clear usage bump as Boston's second option, more so when Paul George sits.

breakouts.name: Rui Hachimura
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). He should see more shots while Brandon Ingram is out and Bradley Beal is limited.

breakouts.name: Derik Queen
breakouts.why: 2 articles across 1 outlet (RotoWire). He posted 17 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists and 2.8 stocks per 36, but may not start next to Zion Williamson and Yves Missi.

breakouts.name: Naz Reid
breakouts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (RotoWire). RotoWire's forwards piece lists him as a breakout in a starting role.

breakouts.name: Ace Bailey
breakouts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (ESPN). His usage climbed to 26% over the final two months of his rookie year; Darryn Peterson's arrival may cost him a starting spot.

breakouts.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
breakouts.why: 1 article across 1 outlet (ESPN). Karabell sees assists and steals upside if he starts; RotoWire lists him as a possible bust because Ty Jerome is ahead of him.

breakouts.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
breakouts.why: Oct 18 preseason check. 15.6 pts, 7.4 reb, 4.0 ast, 1.2 stl, 0.8 blk, 1.2 TO on 56.9% FG in 23 min over 5 games. Penciled in as a starter with Butler and Moody out; Kerr: "He's going to play a ton." FT% (65%) is the weak spot and minutes may shrink when Butler returns.

role_changes.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
role_changes.change: Traded from Milwaukee to Miami in June. He now shares the frontcourt with Bam Adebayo, which raises overlap concerns for both.

role_changes.name: LeBron James
role_changes.change: Signed with Philadelphia in July and joins Embiid, Maxey and Jaylen Brown, so every 76er takes a usage cut.

role_changes.name: Jaylen Brown
role_changes.change: Traded from Boston to Philadelphia for Paul George. He goes from a 35% usage first option to one of four stars.

role_changes.name: Paul George
role_changes.change: Came to Boston in the Jaylen Brown trade as Jayson Tatum's running mate.

role_changes.name: Kawhi Leonard
role_changes.change: Traded from the Clippers back to Toronto for Brandon Ingram. NBC Sports says he was fined for cap circumvention but not suspended.

role_changes.name: Brandon Ingram
role_changes.change: Traded to the Clippers for Kawhi Leonard, then found to have a partially torn Achilles; out to start the season.

role_changes.name: LaMelo Ball
role_changes.change: Traded from Charlotte to Minnesota to run the point next to Anthony Edwards.

role_changes.name: Coby White
role_changes.change: Inherits Charlotte's lead guard role on a three-year, $74 million deal after LaMelo Ball left.

role_changes.name: Brandon Miller
role_changes.change: Becomes the first option with Ball and Miles Bridges gone.

role_changes.name: Naz Reid
role_changes.change: Traded from Minnesota to Charlotte and moves from sixth man to starting power forward.

role_changes.name: Miles Bridges
role_changes.change: Traded from Charlotte to Phoenix.

role_changes.name: Julius Randle
role_changes.change: Moved from Minnesota to Brooklyn, where he should see high usage with Michael Porter Jr.

role_changes.name: Ja Morant
role_changes.change: Traded from Memphis to Portland for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray; he may come off the bench behind Lillard and Holiday.

role_changes.name: Damian Lillard
role_changes.change: Back in Portland after missing 2025-26 with a torn Achilles; he says he will start with Morant and Avdija.

role_changes.name: Ty Jerome
role_changes.change: Has the inside track to start at point guard for Memphis after the Morant trade.

role_changes.name: Cameron Boozer
role_changes.change: The No. 3 pick is expected to be Memphis's primary scorer from day one.

role_changes.name: Walker Kessler
role_changes.change: Signed a four-year, $130 million deal with the Lakers and becomes Luka Doncic's starting center.

role_changes.name: Austin Reaves
role_changes.change: Moves up to second option with LeBron James gone.

role_changes.name: Kyrie Irving
role_changes.change: Returns from a torn ACL after missing 2025-26, under new head coach Dusty May.

role_changes.name: Derrick White
role_changes.change: Becomes Boston's second scoring option after the Jaylen Brown trade.

role_changes.name: Mitchell Robinson
role_changes.change: Signed a three-year deal with Boston and competes with Neemias Queta for the starting center job.

role_changes.name: Josh Hart
role_changes.change: Should start and play heavy minutes with Robinson gone; Andre Drummond backs up Karl-Anthony Towns.

role_changes.name: Nic Claxton
role_changes.change: Traded from Brooklyn to Chicago in June as the Bulls' starting center.

role_changes.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
role_changes.change: Becomes Brooklyn's starting center after the Claxton trade.

role_changes.name: Norman Powell
role_changes.change: Left Miami and joined Chicago's starting lineup.

role_changes.name: Kel'el Ware
role_changes.change: Went from Miami to Milwaukee in the Giannis trade and is out of Bam Adebayo's shadow.

role_changes.name: Tyler Herro
role_changes.change: Moved to Milwaukee in the Giannis trade and is expected to be the main option alongside Ryan Rollins.

role_changes.name: Jaime Jaquez Jr.
role_changes.change: Moved to Milwaukee in the Giannis trade and should start.

role_changes.name: Trae Young
role_changes.change: Acquired by Washington in January and now runs pick-and-roll for Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr.

role_changes.name: Anthony Davis
role_changes.change: Traded to Washington last season without playing a game there; Deandre Ayton was signed as frontcourt cover.

role_changes.name: Darius Garland
role_changes.change: Traded from Cleveland to the Clippers last season for James Harden and is now the lead playmaker with Ingram out.

role_changes.name: Isaiah Jackson
role_changes.change: Has the inside track to start at center for the Clippers over Brook Lopez.

role_changes.name: Peyton Watson
role_changes.change: Joined Cleveland from Denver in August and is likely to start.

role_changes.name: DeMar DeRozan
role_changes.change: Signed with Denver and moves to a reserve role at 37.

role_changes.name: Cameron Johnson
role_changes.change: More minutes and shots after Tim Hardaway Jr. left for Miami and Peyton Watson was dealt.

role_changes.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
role_changes.change: Starts at point guard for Sacramento after Russell Westbrook and DeMar DeRozan departed.

role_changes.name: Domantas Sabonis
role_changes.change: Usage should rise on a rebuilding Kings team, but he and Zach LaVine are reportedly on the trade block.

role_changes.name: Ajay Mitchell
role_changes.change: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe left Oklahoma City, opening wing minutes for Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Jared McCain.

role_changes.name: Jaden McDaniels
role_changes.change: Bigger offensive role with Julius Randle and Naz Reid gone; Jonathan Kuminga signed for two years and $13 million.

role_changes.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
role_changes.change: Traded to Utah last season and now anchors the frontcourt with Walker Kessler gone.

role_changes.name: Ivica Zubac
role_changes.change: Starts his first full season as Indiana's center after a midseason trade from the Clippers.

role_changes.name: Jonathan Kuminga
role_changes.change: Signed with Minnesota after splitting last season between Golden State and Atlanta.

role_changes.name: Bucks rookies (Nate Ament, Brayden Burries)
role_changes.change: New head coach Taylor Jenkins implied both rookies will be brought along slowly; RotoWire would not draft them in redraft.

role_changes.name: Cameron Boozer
role_changes.change: Named the starting PF; team-high 29 min in the Oct 16 finale. Preseason: 14 pts, 5.5 reb, 6 FTA a game at 83% in 20 min, but 2 steals and 0 blocks in 4 games.

role_changes.name: Dylan Harper
role_changes.change: Confirmed opening-night starter: Mitch Johnson plans to start Fox, Harper, Castle, Vassell and Wembanyama.

role_changes.name: Ryan Rollins
role_changes.change: Starting PG with Giannis gone; 27.3% usage with Giannis off the floor last year. Board projects 28 min after 32 last season, so the projection looks low.

role_changes.name: Ausar Thompson
role_changes.change: Bickerstaff plans more minutes; RotoWire projects about 30 against the board's 27. In 40 games of 28+ min last year: 2.2 stl and 1.4 blk.

role_changes.name: Walker Kessler
role_changes.change: Presumptive starting C: 11 pts, 9 reb in 16 min in his Oct 13 debut; Redick: "a great fit for our team."

role_changes.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
role_changes.change: Expected starting C with Claxton in Chicago; ADP up from 82 to 72. Board projects only 22 min.

role_changes.name: Brandin Podziemski
role_changes.change: Starting with Butler (out until early 2027) and Moody (Jan-Feb) out.

role_changes.name: VJ Edgecombe
role_changes.change: Correction Oct 18: the Inquirer reports Nick Nurse used his regular starting lineup (Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, LeBron, Embiid) in the Oct 16 finale; Caldwell-Pope is expected off the bench. An earlier snippet saying KCP started over him was wrong.

role_changes.name: Kel'el Ware
role_changes.change: Projected opener five has Turner and Kuzma starting; expect a bench role around 24 min with strong rebound and block rates.

role_changes.name: Khaman Maluach
role_changes.change: Started the Oct 16 finale, but Ighodaro sat that game and Ott says he will be ready for the opener; the C job is a coin flip.

role_changes.name: Collin Gillespie
role_changes.change: Not in the finale starting five; likely a bench threes-and-assists player after 58 starts last year.

rookies.name: Cameron Boozer
rookies.outlook: No. 3 pick and the highest rookie ADP at about 58. He is expected to be Memphis's primary scorer and offensive hub after averaging 22.5 points and 10.2 rebounds at Duke with 39.1% from three.

rookies.name: AJ Dybantsa
rookies.outlook: No. 1 pick with a big role on a fast-paced Wizards team next to Trae Young and Anthony Davis; ADP is about 75 to 79.

rookies.name: Caleb Wilson
rookies.outlook: No. 4 pick and starting power forward. He brings rebounds, steals and blocks and hit 41.9% from three in Summer League, but FantasyPros flags poor free throws and 5.2 turnovers, so pair him with strong free-throw shooters.

rookies.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
rookies.outlook: No. 7 pick who should start at point guard with 30-plus minutes. Points, assists and threes are there, but he shot 35% in Summer League, so take him after you have field-goal percentage covered.

rookies.name: Darryn Peterson
rookies.outlook: No. 2 pick locked in as a starter beside Keyonte George, with threes and steals; he shares the ball with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

rookies.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
rookies.outlook: No. 11 pick, age 24 and Summer League MVP. Steve Kerr says he will play a ton, and injuries to Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porzingis open minutes at forward and center.

rookies.name: Keaton Wagler
rookies.outlook: No. 5 pick at an ADP near 119. Ty Lue promised on-ball chances with Brandon Ingram and Max Strus out, and NBC Sports sees 30-plus minutes early.

rookies.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
rookies.outlook: No. 6 pick expected to start at point guard, but he is an inefficient shooter and has not played in the preseason because of an ankle injury.

rookies.name: Kingston Flemings
rookies.outlook: No. 8 pick who opens as CJ McCollum's backup with a path to more; steals are his best category.

rookies.name: Hannes Steinbach
rookies.outlook: No. 14 pick and an elite college rebounder competing with Moussa Diabate and Ryan Kalkbrenner for Charlotte's center minutes.

rookies.name: Aday Mara
rookies.outlook: Rookie center who has started preseason games while Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein sit; NBC Sports calls him a possible value.

rookies.name: Nate Ament
rookies.outlook: Expected to be brought along slowly; RotoWire would not target him in redraft. He also has a sprained ankle.

strategy_notes.point: In head-to-head category leagues, aim to dominate six categories instead of being decent at nine.
Centers are the scarcest position, then forwards; guards with upside are easier to find late, so take centers and forwards early. F/C eligibility is the most valuable, then G/F.
Switch from avoiding downside to chasing upside around picks 70 to 90 (rounds 6 to 8); after pick 100 take only upside you could not replace off waivers.

Treat a player as injury-prone when he has five or more seasons under 65 games: Kawhi Leonard (10), Joel Embiid (10), Brandon Ingram (8), Paul George (8), Stephen Curry (7), Zion Williamson (6), LeBron James (6), Jaren Jackson Jr. (5).
Age 33 and older should raise concern: from 2021-22 on, no age group 33 or older produced more than five fantasy-relevant qualifiers in a season.
Only take an injury-risk star after he has fallen about two rounds below ADP; Barutha would take Kawhi Leonard near pick 45, not at his ADP near 30.
The new draft lottery removes most of the tanking incentive, so stars on bad teams face fewer late-season shutdowns in your playoff weeks; four teams played at a sub-15-win pace last March and April.
ADP differs by platform, so use the one for your site: Jaylen Brown goes 30.0 on Yahoo and 42.8 on Fantrax, and LeBron James 37.5 versus 55.0.
Picks 5 through 15 are close this year; break ties by games-played floor first, then category fit, then ADP momentum.
If you reach round 5 with no center, expect to spend rounds 5 and 6 on two of them; Barutha reached for Kel'el Ware at 59 and took Zach Edey at 62.
Picking near the turn forces reaches because 20-plus players go between your picks; Barutha took Kyrie Irving at 38 because he would not last 21 more picks.
Do not lock in a punt before the draft: Cooper Flagg in round 1 needs no punt, and Tyrese Haliburton or Kevin Durant in round 2 rule out punting threes.
Nikola Jokic, Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander hold elite value in every punt build.
Blocks are scarce enough that you may not need to punt them: only 27 qualified players averaged one block last season and only Wembanyama averaged two.
Punt FT% builds start with Giannis Antetokounmpo or Luka Doncic and add Scottie Barnes, Alperen Sengun, Evan Mobley, Donovan Clingan, Rudy Gobert and the Thompson twins.
Punt-assists builds raise frontcourt value; Chet Holmgren, Donovan Clingan and Jalen Duren should all be gone within the first 50 picks of a 12-team draft.
Punting turnovers in 9-cat lifts high-usage playmakers such as Luka Doncic, Cade Cunningham, LaMelo Ball, Trae Young and James Harden.
Second-year players with a new opportunity are the most reliable breakout candidates, and scarce stats (steals, blocks) win category leagues.
Draft a team's clear top-three options, because when one is hurt the other two absorb the usage.
Category value differs from points value: Paolo Banchero and Josh Giddey are better in points leagues, while Kyrie Irving's efficiency and low turnovers make him better in categories.
Take Dyson Daniels only if your first five picks already cover threes and free throws; he gives 2.0 steals but 0.3 threes on 61.5% from the line.
Draft rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. only after securing field-goal percentage, and pair Caleb Wilson with strong free-throw shooters.

Of the stars returning from major injury, NBC Sports rates Haliburton, Tatum, Irving, Lillard, Kessler and Dejounte Murray a full go, VanVleet a likely minutes restriction, and Lively not draftable outside deep leagues.
Role stability matters more than season-long averages for week-to-week H2H lineups; Kel'el Ware's shifting minutes made him hard to start in 2025-26.
